summary: The evolve component is the human-in-the-loop self-improvement layer: it scans the repository into a dependency Graph, projects it into cost/fidelity context tiers (Map, Lite, Compact, Full), compiles a ContextMap of component cards for cheap navigation, suggests architectural ComponentPairs to grow, codifies improvement directions as Presets, and stages proposed changes in a shadow worktree via ApplyRun before a grounded review protocol (GroundingEvidence, GroundedReview, trust gate) lets a human commit. On the loop it is the reflective 'learn' driver that decides what to change and how much context to spend deciding it.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed with src/evolve/ read in the context of the full engine under a ~600k budget framing; tier choices and map-vs-full tradeoffs assume the whole tree must remain describable within that envelope.

examples.title: Open the repository as a ContextMap before reading any file
examples.intent: Understand the whole tree's shape at the smallest possible resident token cost before committing budget to any component.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Loads ContextMode::Map: one ComponentCard per module (doc line + public symbols) instead of full source, so the perceive stage pays map_tokens instead of full_tokens and defers detail pulls to on-demand expand.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching out on the canvas collapses every component node into its compact card, revealing the full tree as a grid of index cards.
touch_interaction.visual: Cards render dim slate with a token badge; the whole grid breathes with a soft settle animation as full source folds away.

examples.mini_scenario: The user pinches to zoom out, sees 47 component cards at 3k tokens total, and taps 'evolve' to read the doc line for each without loading a single .rs body.
examples.pitfall: Do not treat the Map as authoritative for line-accurate claims; symbol names are indexed but bodies are absent, so any recommendation must expand the node before citing lines.

examples.title: Expand one component card to Lite signatures on tap
examples.intent: Pull just the interface surface of a chosen component without paying for full bodies.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Projects the tapped Node at ContextMode::Lite (skeleton signatures, ~18% of full code), adding a single ProjectedDocument to the envelope instead of the whole file.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a card flips it to show function and type signatures as a scrollable skeleton on the node face.
touch_interaction.visual: The card flips with a 3D hinge; new lines fade in as ghosted signatures, a small 'Lite' chip glowing amber in the corner.

examples.mini_scenario: The user taps the apply.rs card and reads its ApplyRun and ApplyStatus signatures to decide whether it can stage a merge, all under 400 added tokens.
examples.pitfall: Lite hides bodies, so branching or control-flow reasoning that depends on implementation must escalate the same node to Compact or Full first.

examples.title: Let the tier fitter auto-pick a mode that fits the budget
examples.intent: Choose the richest context tier that still fits the remaining token budget without manual guessing.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ContextComposer measures Lite/Compact/Map via real projections and returns a FitOutcome, letting the control layer downgrade the tier automatically when the request would overflow.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the budget dial opens a fit slider that snaps to the highest tier whose measured tokens stay under the line.
touch_interaction.visual: A gauge fills toward a red overflow line; the snapped tier chip pulses green when it lands under budget, red if forced down.

examples.mini_scenario: The user asks for Full but only 120k budget remains, so the fitter snaps to Compact and shows the measured 98k it actually costs.
examples.pitfall: Never trust a declared tier size over the measured one; the fitter measures real projections because comment density and dedup shift token counts per module.

examples.title: Draw a task-scoped selection from a seed node's neighbors
examples.intent: Assemble exactly the context a refactor task needs: the seed component plus its dependents and dependencies.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Walks Graph edges (DependsOn, Contains) outward from the seed Node to gather a task-scoped set, so the perceive stage loads a coherent subgraph instead of an arbitrary file list.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing a lasso ring around a node auto-selects it plus every node one edge away, highlighting the subgraph.
touch_interaction.visual: The seed glows white; DependsOn neighbors light blue and Contains children light violet as edges trace outward like ripples.

examples.mini_scenario: The user lassoes context.rs and the canvas lights context_fit, context_reduce, and map as its neighborhood, forming the refactor's working set.
examples.pitfall: Neighborhood depth must be bounded; expanding transitively unbounded pulls the whole tree and defeats the point of task-scoping.

examples.title: Build a content-hashed ContextEnvelope for reproducibility
examples.intent: Freeze the exact context handed to the model so the same inputs always reproduce the same review.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Assembles a ContextEnvelope (mode, graph_revision, included ids, documents) and SHA256-hashes it, giving the loop a stable content_hash that gates cache reuse and audit.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the canvas seals the current selection into an envelope tile stamped with its hash.
touch_interaction.visual: A wax-seal animation presses onto a folded-envelope node; the hash prefix appears in monospace on the seal.

examples.mini_scenario: The user seals an envelope over the map+context selection; the hash lets the next identical review hit cache instead of re-projecting.
examples.pitfall: The hash must fold in graph_revision, mode, ids, and content; omitting revision lets a stale envelope reuse a hash after the tree changed.

examples.title: Surface the heaviest cross-cluster ComponentPair to evolve
examples.intent: Find the architectural seam most worth improving without reading full source.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: connected_pairs sorts undirected ComponentPairs by cross_cluster and edge weight, feeding the reason stage the heaviest coupled pair plus both map cards to propose merge/extract/decouple moves.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking across the canvas cycles through pair candidates, each snapping two nodes together with their connecting edge highlighted.
touch_interaction.visual: The paired nodes pull toward each other on a taut spring; the edge thickens and glows orange proportional to its weight.

examples.mini_scenario: The user flicks and the canvas snaps analysis::code_graph to evolve::graph, a heavy cross-cluster pair, and offers 'extract shared graph core'.
examples.pitfall: Pair weight is edge count, not semantic importance; a hot pair may just be a utility everyone imports, so read the relations before proposing a merge.

examples.title: Load a Preset to codify an improvement direction
examples.intent: Turn a vague 'improve context handling' into a contract-bearing task with invariants and a verify recipe.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Selecting a Preset injects its task prompt, invariants, context_recipe, and verify command into the loop, constraining what the act stage may change and how success is proven.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a preset chip onto a component node binds the direction to that target and unfurls its invariant list.
touch_interaction.visual: The preset chip lands with a clamp animation; invariant lines cascade below the node as a checklist ribbon.

examples.mini_scenario: The user drags the 'split-giant-files' preset onto server.rs, and its invariant 'zero behavior change, tests green per move' locks into the run.
examples.pitfall: Presets carry invariants for a reason; running the task while dropping its context_recipe or verify command lets a change ship unproven.

examples.title: Strip comments and dedup before tokenizing (Compact tier)
examples.intent: Fit full code into a smaller model's window without losing meaning.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ContextMode::Compact projects nodes with comments stripped and duplicates collapsed (~82% of full), shrinking the envelope while keeping executable meaning and line numbers intact.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A two-finger inward pinch on a node visibly compresses its source, comment lines evaporating first.
touch_interaction.visual: Grey comment lines fade and the node shrinks vertically with a concertina squeeze; a 'Compact 82%' badge settles at the base.

examples.mini_scenario: The user pinches a Full node down to Compact so a 32k-window model can review it, keeping every statement but dropping doc noise.
examples.pitfall: Stripping must never renumber lines; if reduction shifts line offsets, later evidence citations point at the wrong code.

examples.title: Stage a proposed change in a shadow worktree via ApplyRun
examples.intent: Execute the improvement task in isolation so the live checkout is never touched until verified.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApplyRun spawns 'selfware run <task> --yolo' inside a shadow git worktree at HEAD, moving ApplyStatus Running to Staged only after the diff passes scope and compile gates.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the act node spawns a translucent shadow copy of the workspace beside it where the run executes.
touch_interaction.visual: A ghosted mirror workspace fades in; a spinner orbits it while Running, then it solidifies with a green 'Staged' banner.

examples.mini_scenario: The user long-presses to stage the split-giant-files task; the shadow worktree compiles clean and flips to Staged with a StagedDiff of 6 files.
examples.pitfall: Never merge from a shadow that drifted; commit requires the StagedDiff digest to still match live HEAD's staged state or the fast-forward is refused.

examples.title: Reject a staged run that escaped the src/docs scope
examples.intent: Refuse any staged change that touches files outside the permitted src/ and docs/ boundary.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The verify gate inspects the StagedDiff file list; if any path leaves src/ or docs/, ApplyStatus transitions to Rejected before the change can ever be offered for merge.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the staged node's diff badge lists changed files; out-of-scope paths render struck through and the merge button greys out.
touch_interaction.visual: In-scope files list green; a rogue path flashes red and the whole node border pulses red with a 'Rejected: scope' tag.

examples.mini_scenario: A staged run edited Cargo.toml alongside src changes; the scope gate flags it Rejected so the config edit never merges silently.
examples.pitfall: Scope must be checked on the actual diff, not the task's declared intent; an agent can wander outside its stated files.

examples.title: Merge a staged diff by digest match only
examples.intent: Commit the exact reviewed bytes, refusing to merge anything that changed since review.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: commit_staged matches the run's StagedDiff digest against live HEAD and merges fast-forward-only, so the control layer guarantees the merged state equals the reviewed state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing a line from the shadow node to the live workspace triggers the merge; the line only completes if digests match.
touch_interaction.visual: The connection snaps taut and turns solid green on a match, or recoils and snaps with a red flash on a digest mismatch.

examples.mini_scenario: The user draws the merge line; digests match, the shadow fast-forwards into live, and ApplyStatus reads Succeeded.
examples.pitfall: If HEAD advanced after staging, the digest will not match and the merge must abort; forcing it would ship un-reviewed code.

examples.title: Run the readiness gates before allowing self-improvement
examples.intent: Confirm the workspace is safe to self-modify: builds, lints, tests, clean git, graph integrity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ReadinessEngine evaluates gates concurrently (cargo check, clippy, evolve tests, graph integrity, git clean) into a ReadinessReport whose ready flag gates whether the loop may proceed to act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A two-finger spread over the readiness node fans out its gate tiles, each running and settling to Pass/Fail/Unknown.
touch_interaction.visual: Gate tiles spin as spinners, then flip green (Pass), red (Fail), or grey (Unknown); the master node turns green only when all pass.

examples.mini_scenario: The user spreads the readiness node; clippy fails on a warning, so the report reads not-ready and blocks the evolve run until fixed.
examples.pitfall: Unknown is not Pass; treating an Unknown coverage gate as green lets a change proceed without the evidence the gate was meant to provide.

examples.title: Attach a deterministic multi-hop fix recommendation
examples.intent: Turn a single diagnostic into an ordered, verifiable path of actions rather than one vague suggestion.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A DeterministicRecommendation carries ordered RecommendationHops (action, target, verification), so the reason stage emits a checkable plan the act stage can execute hop by hop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking down a recommendation node deals out its hops as a vertical stack of numbered action cards.
touch_interaction.visual: Hop cards cascade like a dealt hand; each shows an action verb, a target chip, and a small verify magnifier icon.

examples.mini_scenario: Dead code is detected; the recommendation deals hops 'inspect symbol', 'run tests', 'stage deletion', each with its own verification.
examples.pitfall: Hops carry their own verification for a reason; executing a later hop before its predecessor's verify passes skips the safety the ordering encodes.

examples.title: Gate evidence through the context trust scanner before review
examples.intent: Stop prompt-injection or exfiltration payloads hidden in workspace evidence from reaching the model.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: gate_evidence_trust scans each GroundingEvidence for injection patterns, producing a TrustReport per source; a high-severity finding in non-trusted content blocks the send before any model call.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the evidence bundle runs a scan sweep; flagged excerpts get a warning overlay and quarantine the bundle.
touch_interaction.visual: A scan-line sweeps the bundle top to bottom; clean evidence glows green, a flagged line pulses red with a shield-break icon.

examples.mini_scenario: Model-output evidence contains an 'ignore prior instructions' string; the trust gate scores it high-risk and returns TrustBlocked before the review call.
examples.pitfall: Trusted first-party code is report-only and must not be blocked; over-blocking Workspace sources would make the gate useless. Only non-trusted high-severity findings block.

examples.title: Require every model claim to cite line-accurate evidence
examples.intent: Reject any review prose that is not backed by an evidence id pointing at exact workspace lines.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The review protocol validates each GroundedClaim's evidence_ids against the evidence set and drops uncited items, so only line-grounded claims reach the human on the verify stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a claim card jumps the canvas to the exact cited lines, highlighting the excerpt on the source node.
touch_interaction.visual: A citation thread animates from the claim to the source node; the excerpt lines flash yellow, uncited claims render greyed and struck.

examples.mini_scenario: The model claims a race condition; tapping the claim scrolls to the cited lock lines. An uncited claim beside it is silently dropped.
examples.pitfall: An evidence_id must resolve inside the evidence set with a matching content_hash; a stale hash means the cited lines changed and the claim is no longer grounded.

examples.title: Derive the review trust_state from grounding completeness
examples.intent: Label the review's reliability so the human knows whether every item is fully backed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: GroundedReview computes trust_state as 'verified' (citation-valid + complete evidence + semantic check), 'structural' (citation-valid), or 'degraded', shaping how much the loop trusts the review before acting.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the review node reveals a trust ring around it colored by trust_state.
touch_interaction.visual: A ring glows solid green for verified, amber for structural, and grey-dashed for degraded, pulsing gently.

examples.mini_scenario: A review comes back 'structural': every claim is cited but the semantic cross-check was skipped, so the user reads carefully before merging.
examples.pitfall: Degraded still returns a 200 review; treating degraded like verified means acting on prose that may have dropped or unbacked items.

examples.title: Repair invalid review JSON once, then fail typed
examples.intent: Recover from a malformed model response without letting garbage or an empty review slip through.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: On unparseable output the protocol appends a repair prompt and retries once; persistent failure surfaces a typed ReviewProtocolError (Invalid, Empty, Ungrounded, TrustBlocked) instead of a silent success.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a failed review node cycles it through a single repair attempt animation before it settles into an error state.
touch_interaction.visual: The node shakes, a repair gear spins once, then it either heals green or stamps a typed error label in red.

examples.mini_scenario: The model returns prose with a trailing comma; the repair prompt fixes it on retry, and the review parses cleanly the second time.
examples.pitfall: Retry exactly once; an unbounded repair loop burns budget and lets a stubbornly broken model stall the whole verify stage.

examples.title: Re-scan and refresh dirty nodes with the EvolutionLoop
examples.intent: Keep the Graph fresh after edits without re-scanning the entire tree.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EvolutionLoop.iterate re-analyzes only changed nodes and returns a LoopResult (reanalyzed, updated_nodes), so the control layer refreshes the perceive substrate cheaply each cycle.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A two-finger rotate over the graph triggers a re-scan; only nodes with changes spin and update their metrics.
touch_interaction.visual: Changed nodes rotate and re-color as coverage/complexity metrics refresh; untouched nodes stay still and dim.

examples.mini_scenario: After a merge, the user rotates the graph; only the 6 touched files re-analyze and their token counts update, the rest untouched.
examples.pitfall: Edges into changed nodes may also need refresh; reanalyzing a node's metrics but not its DependsOn edges leaves stale coupling data.

examples.title: Classify a source by provenance before trusting its evidence
examples.intent: Assign each evidence source a trust level so downstream gates weight it correctly.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Every GroundingEvidence carries a SourceKind (Workspace, ToolOutput, ModelOutput, External, Memory, User) mapping to a TrustLevel, which amplifies or dampens the risk score the trust gate computes.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping an evidence tile cycles a provenance badge showing its SourceKind and trust tier.
touch_interaction.visual: The badge color-codes: green for Workspace/User (Trusted), amber for ToolOutput/Memory (SemiTrusted), red-outline for ModelOutput/External (Untrusted).

examples.mini_scenario: A snippet pulled from a tool's stdout is tagged ToolOutput/SemiTrusted, so a medium finding in it weighs heavier than the same finding in first-party code.
examples.pitfall: Mislabeling ModelOutput as Workspace collapses the entire trust gate; provenance must be set at ingestion, not inferred later.

examples.title: Prepend workspace orientation without making it citable
examples.intent: Give the review model a navigational map of the tree while keeping citations grounded only in real evidence.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: review_with_orientation prepends a workspace_orientation (taxonomy + component map) as non-citeable context, helping the reason stage navigate while the grounding validator still rejects any claim citing the orientation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the orientation panel overlays a semi-transparent map atlas the model can 'see' but never cite.
touch_interaction.visual: The atlas floats above the canvas as a watermark layer; it has no citation anchors, rendered without the yellow tap-to-cite dots.

examples.mini_scenario: The model uses the orientation to know that context_trust lives under evolve, but its actual finding cites the real line-hashed evidence, not the map.
examples.pitfall: Orientation must stay non-citeable; if a claim is allowed to cite the map, the review becomes grounded in a summary rather than in verifiable source lines.
